chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Muhammad ibn Jamhur from Ahmad ibn al-Fadl from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman who said:

Abu Ibrahim (Imam al-Kadhim, peace be upon him) passed away, and there was no one among his representatives (quwwam) except that he had a large amount of wealth. This was the reason for their Waqifiyyah stance and their denial of his death, out of greed for the money. Ziyad ibn Marwan al-Qandi possessed seventy thousand dinars, and Ali ibn Abi Hamza possessed thirty thousand dinars. When I saw this and the truth became clear to me, and I recognized the matter of Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) as I knew it, I spoke up and called people to his Imamate. Then they sent two messengers to me and said: 'What is calling you to this? If you desire wealth, we will make you independent (rich)!' They guaranteed me ten thousand dinars and said to me: 'Refrain.' I refused and said to them: 'We have narrated from the Two Truthful Imams (peace be upon them) that they said: When innovations appear, it is upon the scholar to manifest his knowledge; if he does not do so, he will be deprived of the light of faith. And I would not abandon jihad and the command of God in any case.' So they antagonized me and harbored enmity against me.

key_terms.الصَّادِقَيْنِ: the Two Truthful (Imam al-Baqir and Imam al-Sadiq)

ai.seo_question: What was the economic reason behind the Waqifiyyah sect's denial of Imam al-Kadhim's death?
ai.summary: This narrative from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman elucidates the economic roots of the Waqifiyyah sect, whose denial of Imam al-Kadhim’s (a.s.) death was driven by the desire to retain control over vast wealth held by their representatives. The narrator’s refusal of a ten-thousand-dinar bribe to remain silent underscores the Shia scholarly principle that maintaining faith requires active opposition to innovation, even at personal cost, thereby securing his standing with Imam al-Rida (a.s.).
